# seo-ai-checker: reviewer context

- **What it is:** "SearchLens" / Search Visibility Checker. A free public tool at tools.rvadigitalworks.com. A visitor enters any website URL, and the server fetches it (plus its /robots.txt, /llms.txt, /sitemap.xml) and returns a 0-100 SEO + AI-searchability score with per-check findings. Deployed on Railway from a PUBLIC GitHub repo, so anything committed is world-readable.
- **Stack:** Node >= 20 ESM (`"type": "module"`), Express 4, Cheerio. There is no database, no session/auth system and no build step. Outbound HTTP goes through Node's global `fetch`, and every outbound page fetch goes through `fetchUrl()` in `lib/fetcher.js` (the one choke point for URL-fetch safety). Only Perplexity (`lib/ai-citation.js`) uses `fetch` directly. Frontend is plain JS in `public/`, served by `express.static` with `extensions: ['html']` (so `/checks` serves `checks.html`). jsPDF and autotable load from cdnjs.
- **HTTP surface (all unauthenticated):** `GET /api/config`, `POST /api/lead`, `POST /api/scan` (JSON `{url}`, single page), and three SSE (`text/event-stream`) routes: `GET /api/scan-site?url=` (crawl up to 25 same-origin pages, concurrency 5), `GET /api/competitors?url=&rivals=` (DuckDuckGo Lite, then DDG HTML, then Bing scraping, plus up to 5 manual rivals), and `GET /api/ai-citation?url=` (Perplexity Agent API, 4 prompts). SSE event names the frontend depends on: `progress`, `status`, `done`, `failed`.
- **Mode switch:** `PUBLIC_MODE` env (`1|true|yes`) turns on the per-IP in-memory rate limits (10 single / 4 heavy scans per hour), the client-side email gate, the hire-us CTA, stripping of the "fix-it prompt" and PDF, and a hard server-side refusal of `/api/ai-citation`. Without it (local/internal use via `Start SearchLens.bat` / `.env`), everything is open and unlimited.
- **Env vars (names are a contract):** `PUBLIC_MODE`, `WEB3FORMS_KEY`, `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`, `PERPLEXITY_MODEL` (default `perplexity/sonar`), `PORT`. `.env` is gitignored, and only `.env.example` with empty values is committed.
- **Intentionally public:** `WEB3FORMS_KEY` is handed to the browser via `/api/config` in public mode, because Web3Forms accepts submissions only from the browser. The Perplexity key must never leave the server (`/api/config` exposes only the boolean `aiCitation`). RVA Digital Works contact email and phone appear in the HTML and PDF footer by design.
- **Data flow of untrusted content:** third-party HTML is parsed server-side only. Report strings derived from it (title, meta description, H1, canonical, lang, charset, schema types) come back in `check.detail`/`check.message`. On the frontend, any field that can carry third-party text must go through `escapeHtml()` (app.js) or `esc()` (ai-citation.js) before `innerHTML`, or be set with `textContent`. Link `href`s use `encodeURI()` on server-produced http(s) URLs. Category `title`/`icon` strings are server constants and are interpolated unescaped.
- **Lead capture:** emails go browser to Web3Forms, plus a fire-and-forget `POST /api/lead` that only `console.log`s to Railway logs. Nothing is persisted server-side. The `?url=<site>&src=quiz` deep link from rvadigitalworks.com's quiz auto-runs a single scan and skips the email gate (contract with the main site).
- **Conventions a change must not break:** the CSP header in `server.js` (connect-src limited to self + api.web3forms.com, script-src self + cdnjs). The report JSON shape used by app.js, report-pdf.js and public-gate.js (`categories[].checks[]`, `topFixes`, `counts`, and site mode's `issues[]`, `pages[]`, `passingEverywhere`). The browser-like User-Agent/Sec-* header set in fetcher.js (comment: bot tokens get blocked by WAFs). Rate-limiter names `scanLimiter`/`heavyLimiter` referenced in DEPLOY.md.
